extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / specialists working on Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory, Frobenioids, and related category-theoretic structures
extracted.subtask_description: Formal specification and local/global properties required to construct Θ-Hodge theaters and related Frobenioid-theoretic objects (log-/tempered-meromorphic functions, Kummer structures, Θ-links, Frobenius-pictures) in the setting of IUT/IUT-type frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition (a) for a meromorphic function on Zlog^∞
rubrics_metrics.description: For every N ∈ N≥1, the meromorphic function f admits an N-th root over some tempered covering of Zlog^∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate implication: (a) ⇒ (b). The theta function of [EtTh] satisfies condition (a) (see (ii)). This is the strongest of the three listed conditions on f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition (b) for a meromorphic function on Zlog^∞
rubrics_metrics.description: For every N ∈ N≥1 which is prime to p, f admits an N-th root over some tempered covering of Zlog^∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We have (a) ⇒ (b) and (b) ⇔ (c). When N is prime to p and (c) holds, admissible coverings theory yields finite log-étale covering Ylog → Zlog whose universal combinatorial covering provides the required tempered covering; thus (c) ⇒ (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition (c) for a meromorphic function on Zlog^∞ (log-divisor condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The divisor of zeroes and poles of f is a log-divisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate: (b) ⇒ (c). Conversely, when N is prime to p, (c) ⇒ (b) via admissible coverings. It is not clear whether (b) or (c) implies the stronger property (a) (author notes uncertainty). [Used in [EtTh] under the name 'log-meromorphic' in Deﬁnition 3.1(ii)].

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation among (a),(b),(c)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explicitly records that (a) implies (b); (b) and (c) are equivalent; but the implication (b) or (c) ⇒ (a) is unclear/unknown to the author at time of writing. This uncertainty affects the correctness of places in [EtTh] where only (c) was assumed but (a) was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation (A): redefine 'log-meromorphic' to require (a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify [EtTh], Deﬁnition 3.1(ii), so that 'log-meromorphic' means the function satisfies condition (a) (i.e., admits N-th roots over tempered coverings for every N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantage: remainder of [EtTh] goes through unchanged; allows Kummer theory of arbitrary rational functions of the tempered Frobenioid without further hypotheses. Author suggests the alternate term 'tempered-meromorphic' might be better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative (B) / Frobenioid-theoretic condition (d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify [EtTh], Deﬁnition 4.1(i), to assume f ∈ O×(Abirat) satisfies: (d) For every N ∈ N≥1, there exists a linear morphism A' → A in C such that the pull-back of f to A' admits an N-th root.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a Frobenioid/category-theoretic condition: linear morphisms and rational function monoid are category-theoretic, so (d) is category-theoretic. Theta functions satisfy (d). Approach (B) avoids changing the notion 'tempered Frobenioid' but slightly reduces the range of applicability of [EtTh], §4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical corrections to the definition of the monoid Φ^ell_W in [EtTh], Example 3.9
rubrics_metrics.description: Three slight modifications to [EtTh], Example 3.9 to avoid irrelevant technical difficulties:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Replace 'Y log is of genus 1' by 'Y log is of genus 1 and has either precisely one cusp or precisely two cusps whose difference is a 2-torsion element of the underlying elliptic curve'. (2) Correct a typographical diagram arrow phrase to '˙X log → ˙C log'. (3) Replace 'unramified over the cusps of ...' with 'unramified over the cusps as well as over the generic points of the irreducible components of the special fibers of the stable models of ...' and 'tempered coverings of the underlying ...' with 'tempered admissible coverings of the underlying ...'. Overall guidance: Φ^ell_W is to be defined 'just large enough' to include precisely those divisors needed for the theta functions in [EtTh].

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstructability of subcategory D^{(4)}_v from D_v
rubrics_metrics.description: The subcategory D^{(4)}_v ⊆ D_v may be reconstructed category-theoretically from D_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as Example 3.3(iii)(a); supports recovery of local data from global category-theoretic structures (cf. [AbsAnab], Lemma 1.3.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstructability of D^{(4)}_v and D^Θ_v from C^{(4)}_v and C^Θ_v
rubrics_metrics.description: The categories D^{(4)}_v (resp. D^Θ_v) may be reconstructed category-theoretically from C^{(4)}_v (resp. C^Θ_v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced Example 3.3(iii)(b); citations: [FrdI], Theorem 3.4(v); [FrdII], Theorem 1.2(1); [AbsAnab], Theorem 1.1.1(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstructability of D_v from the Frobenioid F_v
rubrics_metrics.description: The category D_v may be reconstructed category-theoretically from F_v (the Frobenioid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.3(iii)(c). This underpins the ability to recover base categories from Frobenioid data (citations in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-theoreticity of the divisor monoid Φ_{C_v}
rubrics_metrics.description: The divisor monoid Φ_{C_v} is category-theoretic and hence, together with previous reconstructability statements, implies that C^{(4)}_v may be reconstructed category-theoretically from F_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.3(iii)(d); references: [FrdI], Corollary 4.11(iii); [FrdII], Theorem 1.2(i); together with (a) and (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of split Frobenioids F^{(4)}_v and F^Θ_v from F_v
rubrics_metrics.description: One may reconstruct, category-theoretically, the split Frobenioids F^{(4)}_v and F^Θ_v associated to Θ (including characteristic splittings τ_v) from F_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.3(iii)(e). The text indicates the characteristic splitting element pv of O_Kv can be constructed algorithmically from F_v, enabling recovery of the split structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer structure κ_v and its equivalent data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kummer structure κ_v : O(2)(C_v) → A D_v is completely equivalent to: (i) the Aut-holomorphic structure (induced by κ_v) on the groupification O(2)(C_v)^{gp}, together with (ii) the tautological co-holomorphicization O(2)(C_v)^{gp} → A D_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.4, Remark 3.4.2. Practical consequence: thinking of κ_v as this pair separates the monoid (non-logarithm-compatible) portion from the co-holomorphicization (logarithm-compatible) portion. The co-holomorphicization is compatible with the logarithm operation (cf. [AbsTopIII], Corollary 4.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of objects of TM(4) for archimedean places
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects of TM(4) are split topological monoids (C, C^×) with compact factor C^× ≅ S^1 and noncompact factor ≅ R_{≥0}, and morphisms must induce compatible isomorphisms on these factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.4(ii). The construction yields topological monoids O(2)(C^{(4)}_v) that split as O^× × Φ_C with Φ_C ≅ R_{≥0}; characteristic splittings τ_v arise accordingly and are part of the split Frobenioid data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-Hodge theater condition (a) (nonarchimedean v ∈ V_non)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ V_non, †F_v is a category admitting an equivalence of categories †F_v ∼→ F_v; in particular †F_v admits a natural Frobenioid structure which is constructible solely from the category-theoretic structure of †F_v. Write †D_v, †D^{(4)}_v, †F^{(4)}_v etc. for the corresponding objects constructed category-theoretically from †F_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.6(a). This requires that the †-objects reproduce the non-† examples (Examples 3.2,3.3) under categorical reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-Hodge theater condition (b) (archimedean v ∈ Varc)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ Varc, †F_v is a triple (†C_v, †D_v, †κ_v) where †C_v is category equivalent to Cv, †D_v is an Aut-holomorphic orbispace, and †κ_v : O(2)(†C_v) → A^{†}D_v is an inclusion of topological monoids (the Kummer structure); there must exist an isomorphism of collections of data between these †-objects and the corresponding non-† objects from Example 3.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.6(b). The existence of the Kummer inclusion †κ_v and equivalence †C_v ∼→ C_v is required; †κ_v must realize the same kind of data as κ_v in the non-† theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-Hodge theater condition (c) (global realified Frobenioid data)
rubrics_metrics.description: †F^{(4)}_{mod} is a collection (†C^{(4)}_{mod}, Prime(†C^{(4)}_{mod}) ∼→ V, {†F^{(4)}_v}_{v∈V}, {†ρ_v}_{v∈V}) where †C^{(4)}_{mod} admits an equivalence to C^{(4)}_{mod}, Prime is a bijection to V, and each †ρ_v : Φ_{†C^{(3)}}_{mod,v} ∼→ Φ^{rlf}_{†C^{(4)}_v} is an isomorphism of topological monoids; also there must exist an isomorphism of collections of data to the corresponding non-† global objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.6(c). This encodes the global compatibility and realification data required for a Θ-Hodge theater.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-Link existence (Corollary 3.7(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Between any two Θ-Hodge theaters †HT_Θ and ‡HT_Θ (relative to same initial Θ-data), the full poly-isomorphism between their global collections of data †F^{(4)}_{tht} ∼→ ‡F^{(4)}_{tht} is nonempty; this full poly-isomorphism is called the Θ-link from †HT_Θ to ‡HT_Θ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 3.7(i). In practice one must produce a poly-isomorphism (possibly many distinct ones) linking the collections; no distinguished choice is conferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-Link preserves D^{(4)} (Corollary 3.7(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each v ∈ V, the Θ-link induces composite (full) poly-isomorphisms †D^{(4)}_v ∼→ †D^{(4),Θ}_v ∼→ ‡D^{(4)}_v, i.e., it preserves the D^{(4)}-type data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 3.7(ii). The tautological isomorphisms (varying with v ∈ V_good or V_bad) combined with the Θ-link give these composites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-Link preserves O^× (Corollary 3.7(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each v ∈ V, relative to the composite isomorphism of (ii), the Θ-link induces composite (full) poly-isomorphisms O^×_{†C^{(4)}_v} ∼→ O^×_{†C^{(4),Θ}_v} ∼→ O^×_{‡C^{(4)}_v}, i.e., it preserves the invertible-section monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 3.7(iii). This compatibility is required for links to be valid; it follows from tautological identifications and the induced poly-isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-picture property of Θ-linked chains (Corollary 3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: An infinite chain of distinct Θ-Hodge theaters linked by Θ-links gives an oriented infinite graph (the 'Frobenius-picture') with a natural Z-translation action; the structure is 'order-conscious' and does not admit arbitrary permutation symmetries (e.g., cannot switch adjacent vertices while fixing others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 3.8. This is a structural constraint on allowable automorphisms of the infinite Θ-linked chain; it motivates referring to the chain as 'Frobenius-like' or 'order-conscious'.
